turns.input: Pellan gives Nicco a pair of leather boots.
turns.narration:
Pellan shuffled his ink-stained fingers against his shabby coat, then bent to unlace the worn leather boots he was carrying. "Here," he said, not quite meeting Nicco's eyes. "They'll do you better than whatever you're wearing now, I'd think." He held them out, spectacles slipping slightly down his thin nose.

The boots were ordinary enough—scuffed, well-used, nothing remarkable about them. Pellan's hand trembled a little as he waited, clearly uncomfortable with the gesture itself rather than any particular doubt about the gift.

turns.input:
Thanks *he said to them, after which he decides to give them back the boots*
You'll need them more than me
turns.narration:
Nicco thanks Pellan, then holds the boots back out toward him. "You'll need them more than me."

A thin, slightly hunched man with messy hair and permanently ink-stained fingers, his thick round spectacles catching the daylight, Pellan blinks behind the lenses. He looks from the boots to Nicco's feet and back again, his brow knitting. "I—well—" He pushes his spectacles up with one stained finger, leaving a faint smudge on the bridge. "They're not meant for me, though. I've already got a pair. These came out of a storage room nobody's claimed in years, so far as the registry shows." He does not move to take them, standing there in his own rumpled, modest clothing with the quiet uncertainty of someone who prepared for one conversation and finds himself in another.
